_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
NI-DAQ pressure and flow now share the native hardware sample clock. Arduino receipt timestamps are captured before GUI delivery.

Arm and Wrist CVP earn additional pump authority for measured rises below 1 mmHg/s. Regional PID gains blend across pressure boundaries. A session-only simulator setting separates pulse-rejected control feedback from raw pressure, recordings and safety. Default is 50 bpm; 0 disables preservation.

Sinusoid diagnostics report measured amplitude, phase lag, bias, RMSE and emitted commands. Generation is blocked while simulator preservation is enabled or unread. Stop the simulator and apply 0 bpm before generating a waveform. Unsupported coherence, THD and stability-margin claims have been removed.

Device D protected flash/restore preserved calibration. Ten-minute seed-213 Arm/Wrist soak: 8 cycles, 100% telemetry delivery; valve reversals 0.141–0.270/s, below the 0.5/s gate. Live NI check retained 9,960 samples on all three channels through a deliberate 2.015-second GUI backlog. Pulse pressure remains visible with little actuator response at 50 bpm; unchanged pneumatic pulse shape is not established by these checks.

Cal 3's five-second rest and independent Kp/Kn fixes from v3.1.253 are included. This unsigned installer may show Windows SmartScreen: More info -> Run anyway. Saved calibration remains protected.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
